Dominion Energy Virginia has filed for a 180-day extension on the Loudoun County 500kV substation upgrade due to transformer procurement delays. Equipment backlog from the primary vendor has pushed the expected energization date from Q3 2025 to Q1 2026. The substation serves the primary interconnection point for three large-load data center facilities in Ashburn, VA currently awaiting commercial operation.

The Office of the Attorney General of Virginia has submitted a formal protest to the State Corporation Commission regarding Dominion Energy's proposed large-load tariff amendments. The protest alleges that the proposed rate structure improperly shifts right-of-way acquisition delay costs from hyperscale data center operators onto residential ratepayers across the Dominion service territory.

American Electric Power filed a system impact study update indicating that the Columbus data center interconnection cluster has withdrawn 24,300 MW of uncommitted capacity requests following implementation of the take-or-pay tariff. Expected commercial operation dates have been extended by an average of 14 months across the affected queue positions. AEP projects that confirmed contracted load has declined from 30,000 MW to 5,700 MW of bankable demand.

The Pennsylvania Public Utility Commission received a formal protest from the Office of Consumer Advocate challenging Constellation Energy's proposed behind-the-meter co-location agreement with a hyperscale data center operator at the Susquehanna nuclear facility. The protest alleges that the arrangement shifts approximately $340M in annual grid maintenance costs to residential ratepayers and requests a formal restudy of the cost-shifting methodology before any tariff approval.

FERC issued a Show Cause order under FPA Section 206 regarding Talen Energy's Cumulus Data co-location arrangement at Susquehanna Steam Electric Station. The Commission identified concerns about net injection configurations and directed Talen to demonstrate compliance within 90 days or face a formal contract restudy. An intervening party representing industrial ratepayers has further alleged that the behind-the-meter arrangement improperly circumvents PJM's interconnection queue process.

FERC received a Section 206 complaint from the PJM Independent Market Monitor alleging that Constellation Energy's proposed nuclear co-location tariff unfairly shifts transmission cost allocation obligations from the co-located data center operator to other PJM market participants. The IMM requests a formal evidentiary hearing and interim injunctive relief pending resolution.
